transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-23 16:00 PST | Duration 52m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Mark (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Raj (CTO), Lina (Head of Security), Evan (Infra), Maya (Compliance)

[00:00] Mark: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick intro — I'm Mark with Redwood inference, and Priya will run the technical bits. how's everyone doing?
[00:12] Raj: Good thanks, sorry for the slight delay, had back-to-back. We're excited to go over the private deployment checklist.
[00:18] Lina: Hi all. main thing for us is SOC2 readiness and ensuring keys and logs are controlled. we have a hard requirement for customer-managed KMS and 365 day audit retention.
[00:28] Priya: Great, thanks Lina. we'll walk through our recommended architecture — we'll call out the airlock/egress pattern we typically use for private VPCs, how KMS integration works, and audit log flows into your SIEM.
[00:39] Evan: Quick practical question: are you supporting a private control plane in our VPC or does the control plane talk out to Redwood? We need to know for egress rules.
[00:49] Mark: Good question — Redwood supports both patterns. For Private deployments we can offer a private control plane that runs in your VPC with no outbound internet allowed except to your KMS endpoint, or a managed control plane where the control plane talks to Redwood's management endpoints. Both have tradeoffs.
[01:04] Lina: For SOC2 we prefer minimal outbound. can you detail what minimal means — port, IPs, TLS, etc.
[01:11] Priya: Sure. For the private control plane, minimal outbound is basically KMS and our telemetry egress if you opt in. If you want zero external egress, we support an air-gapped mode where audit and metrics are pushed to your SIEM and you host the control plane. In the managed model we provide an allowlist of IPs and FQDNs over TLS 443.
[01:28] Raj: And cert management — does Redwood terminate TLS or do we? we need mTLS to the agents ideally.
[01:35] Priya: We support customer-provided certs. For inter-service comms within your VPC we recommend mTLS with your PKI or using client certs issued by your CA; Redwood can validate. For the managed endpoints, TLS is terminated by Redwood at the edge, but all data in transit is encrypted.
[01:50] Evan: About KMS: we use AWS KMS in our prod account and GCP KMS in a few regions. can Redwood integrate with both and allow key rotation policies?
[01:58] Priya: Yes. Redwood's private deploy supports AWS KMS and GCP KMS. We do a sign-and-wrap pattern: customer keys perform envelope encryption, Redwood stores wrapped keys. Rotation flows are supported — we have documented steps. we'll share the exact API calls and IAM roles.
[02:14] Lina: Do you ever store plaintext keys? that's a hard no for us.
[02:18] Priya: No plaintext keys are stored. we only store wrapped keys and key references. at rest, model artifacts are encrypted with keys that are wrapped by the customer KMS — we only persist the wrapped blob.
[02:29] Raj: How do you handle key compromise or rotation? is there an emergency revoke?
[02:33] Priya: If a key is revoked, you instruct KMS to disable unwrap; Redwood's runtime will fail to decrypt token blobs and attempts will error. for emergency flows we support key re-wrap and a rolling re-encrypt procedure; we'll provide scripts for that.
[02:47] Maya: On audit logs: we need immutable logs sent to our SIEM with at least 365 days retention and WORM where possible. What fields do you emit?
[02:56] Priya: We emit request metadata: timestamp, model id, route, user token id (hashed), request size, response size, latency, node id, and for admin actions we log user id, action, and outcome. We can also add custom fields if you map your SSO identities.
[03:12] Lina: Do you support ingest to S3 with server-side encryption and object-lock for WORM?
[03:17] Priya: Yes, we can push logs to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS and object lock. Alternatively we can stream to your SIEM via syslog/HTTPS.
[03:26] Evan: For network egress controls — what does the airlock look like? do you recommend a NAT + proxy or a purpose-built egress proxy appliance?
[03:35] Priya: Typical pattern we see: inside the VPC you run the runtime nodes in private subnets. outbound calls must pass through a hardened egress proxy — we recommend an egress proxy that supports allowlists, TLS inspection if required, and mutual auth to services like KMS. Some customers use a Layer 7 firewall with limited rules, others prefer a small fleet of bastion proxies with strict logging.
[03:55] Raj: Are there built-in RBAC hooks to map our Okta groups to Redwood roles?
[04:00] Mark: Yes — we support SAML/OIDC SSO and can ingest group claims. You can map Okta group names to roles in the Redwood Console or via config API, giving you RBAC for who can deploy models, who can view logs, etc.
[04:12] Lina: We also need separation between model operators and auditors. auditors should only see logs, not model prompts.
[04:18] Priya: We can redact PII and redact prompt bodies for auditor roles; logs can contain metadata only for auditors. We also support token-level redaction policies.
[04:30] Evan: Latency question — if we force all KMS calls through a proxy in our VPC, will that impact inference latency during key unwrap at cold start?
[04:38] Priya: The unwrap happens infrequently; we cache unwrapped keys in an encrypted KV cache in memory. Cold start may add a small overhead on the first request; we recommend a warmup hook to rotate and prefetch keys during deployment. For token-by-token operations we avoid repeated KMS calls.
[04:58] Raj: About the private control plane: if we run it in our VPC, how do updates and rollouts work? can Redwood push updates or is it a manual pull?
[05:07] Priya: There are two modes. In managed-private mode, the control plane nodes can pull updates from a signed Redwood artifact repository — you can either allow egress to that repo or host a mirrored artifact store inside your network. We also support an airgap workflow where you pull upgrade artifacts into an internal repo and then apply them.
[05:26] Lina: On SOC2 evidence — what artifacts do you have readily available?
[05:31] Mark: We can provide SOC2 Type II attestation, a security whitepaper, list of subservice org responsibilities, SOC mapping spreadsheet, incident response runbook, and our RBAC/SSO config guide. I'll attach those.
[05:44] Maya: Please include any pen test reports and a table of encryption-in-transit/in-rest enforcement.
[05:50] Priya: We also have a procedural document for key rotation and revoked key handling we will share.
[05:56] Raj: Regarding egress allowlists — can you provide a minimal CIDR/IP list? we have a very strict firewall.
[06:03] Mark: For managed endpoints we provide a small set of IPs and FQDNs; for the private control plane there's essentially no outbound if you choose the internal KMS path. We'll provide an allowlist spreadsheet.
[06:15] Evan: More on telemetry — if we turn off telemetry, do we lose observability for performance troubleshooting?
[06:20] Priya: Minimal telemetry is needed for internal autoscaling. If you opt out completely we can still run with local metrics and you can ship metrics to your own Prometheus/SIEM. It's a tradeoff: fully turned off limits Redwood ability to proactively detect regressions.
[06:36] Lina: What about data residency — we must ensure all data for EU customers stays in EU. how do you ensure model artifacts and logs sit in region?
[06:45] Priya: In private deployments you control the region and storage. For hosted models we offer region pinning; we also maintain separate storage endpoints per region. For private you can force all storage and compute in your EU accounts and use EU KMS keys.
[06:58] Raj: Are there any FIPS or HSM integration options? we have an HSM requirement for certain keys.
[07:05] Priya: We integrate with HSM-backed KMS via supported cloud KMS offerings and can integrate with on-prem HSMs over standard KMIP in some setups. We'll need to map specifics in the pilot.
[07:17] Evan: For firewalling: do you recommend stateful rules or a next-gen FW? also curious about connections between model nodes — do they need to talk outbound to the internet for tokenizer updates or model pulls?
[07:28] Priya: Model pulls are only required at deploy time. You can host model artifacts in an internal object store so nodes never touch the internet. For runtime, internal node-to-node traffic should be limited to private subnets with security groups (stateful) and we recommend a NGFW at the perimeter for inspection.
[07:44] Lina: Any guidance for segmentation between dev/test and prod? we want strict separation.
[07:48] Priya: Definitely separate accounts and VPCs for prod and non-prod. Use separate KMS keys and ensure no cross-account roles exist. We also recommend separate SIEM spaces and different object stores.
[07:59] Raj: Let's talk about a concrete pilot — what minimal pieces do you need from us to stand up a private instance?
[08:05] Mark: Minimal: a VPC CIDR and subnets, an S3-compatible bucket for model artifacts, KMS key ARN(s), an IAM role with limited privileges for the runtime, and egress rules for KMS if you choose external KMS. Evan, if you can export firewall rules and CIDRs that will help Priya size the deployment.
[08:21] Evan: I can get that by Friday.
[08:24] Maya: For legal, we need a DPA; who is our legal contact?
[08:28] Mark: I'll connect Maya to our legal team — I'll send the contact after the call.
[08:33] Priya: A quick callout — for artifacts we recommend enabling request-level hashing so raw prompts aren't stored unless you opt in. That helps with privacy review.
[08:43] Lina: Good. also want to confirm: RBAC for Console actions and API keys — can we rotate and audit API keys?
[08:50] Priya: Yes, API keys can be rotated via the Console or API and key creation/usage is logged. We also support short-lived tokens integrated with your STS system.
[08:59] Raj: Any gotchas with on-prem GPUs? some of our nodes are older hardware.
[09:05] Priya: Older GPUs might need specific builds or quantized model variants. For private on-prem we'll do a compatibility matrix — Priya will run a small compatibility benchmark.
[09:17] Evan: How about network egress for telemetry if we want to keep things internal? can you publish a telemetry collector image we run that forwards to Redwood over a TLS tunnel?
[09:27] Priya: Yes, we have a telemetry agent image. You can run it behind your proxy and either forward to Redwood, or to your own metrics backend; if you prefer a push model to your SIEM we can support that too.
[09:40] Speaker 1: (audio glitch) sorry, dropped for a sec.
[09:44] Mark: No worries — quick recap: we'll send SOC artifacts, KMS guide, and allowlist. Priya will send the onboarding checklist and sample network diagram. Customer will send firewall rules and KMS ARNs.
[09:58] Raj: Sounds good. Let's plan to start the pilot week of Dec 6th.
[10:03] Lina: One last question: do you provide attestation for encrypted backups and backup restore process?
[10:10] Priya: Backups are encrypted with customer keys (when configured) and restore requires key unwrap. We'll include backup/restore steps in the security doc.
[10:17] Mark: Great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the docs and next steps.
[10:22] Maya: Thanks — appreciate the thoroughness.
[10:25] (meeting ends)
